title: DMW monitors OFWs in Japan after magnitude-5.7 earthquake
summary: The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) has said it is monitoring the condition of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Japan following a magnitude-5.7 earthquake early Sunday, November 8, 2026.

blocks.text: The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) has said it is monitoring the condition of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Japan following a magnitude-5.7 earthquake early Sunday, November 8, 2026.

Citing the Japan Meteorological Agency, the DMW said the earthquake originated in Shizuoka Prefecture at a depth of about 40 kms. Its tremors reportedly affected Hamamatsu and parts of Aichi, Kyoto, Nara, Yamanashi, and Gifu.
Smaller aftershocks followed the earthquake, but no tsunami warning was issued. Meanwhile, at least 22 people were reportedly injured.
The DMW said it is carrying out monitoring efforts in coordination with its Migrant Workers Office (MWO) and the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) in Tokyo.

"The MWO and OWWA in Tokyo are coordinating with the Philippine Embassy and relevant Japanese authorities to check on the condition of Filipinos in the affected areas and determine whether assistance is needed," the agency said in an advisory issued Monday.

"The DMW advises OFWs and other Filipino nationals in central Japan and nearby areas to remain alert for possible aftershocks, follow official safety advisories, and prepare essential supplies," it added.
The agency also urged OFWs to identify designated evacuation sites and stay clear of areas prone to landslides or rockfalls, particularly during heavy rains.
